text.p: Britain's third largest supermarket group Safeway on Thursday upped the stakes in the battle for customer loyalty by teaming up with high-street bank Abbey National to offer banking services via its ABC card.

Safeway's link with Abbey follows moves by rivals Tesco Plc and J. Sainsbury Plc into financial services, which have become the latest weapon in the food superstores struggle to win supremacy in Britain's fiercely competitive retail market.
The tie-up with Abbey was seen by analysts as a positive move for Safeway, capitalising on its strengths in customer service and technology.

"It's a good deal," said David McCarthy, food retailing analyst at Barclays de Zoete Wedd. "It's an extension of customer services and they are exploiting the lead they have in technology over the competition."
News of the link helped push Safeway's shares to a three and a half year high, gaining 8.5 pence to 388.5 pence.
The move is expected to enhance profits, but the key issue is the lead it gives the group in terms of customer service, other analysts said.
"The Abbey National deal continues to show Safeway wants to be at the forefront of marketing in the sector," said a food retail analyst, who asked to remain anonymous.

Safeway's card is more advanced than Tesco's Clubcard Plus deposit facility, but less ambitious than Sainsbury's Bank, a partnership with Bank of Scotland, offering full blown deposit, lending and cash management services.

Food retailers are not alone in branching out into banking. Clothing retailer Marks and Spencer Plc is a well-established player, selling insurance, personal loans and savings products such as PEPs (personal equity plans).
Analysts see this diversification as part of a long term trend where retailers are increasingly trying to exploit inefficiencies in other markets.

For Abbey National, formerly a building society and still a major force in home loans, the deal will give it an entirely new customer base. All 5.6 million of Safeway's ABC cardholders will be eligible to apply for the Bonus Account.

"We have been developing a joint strategy with Safeway for some time and welcome the opportunity to work closely with a leading retailer which has a similar customer focus to our own," Abbey National chief executive Peter Birch said.
The new card will initially offer customers a deposit account, but is set to be followed by a debit card with overdraft facility, a credit card and a range of other financial services.

Shoppers can use the card to pay for goods and services in other retail chains, including C&A, Granada, Lillywhites, Virgin and W.H. Smith. Safeway said it would be accepted at 70,000 outlets which take Visa's Electron debit card. Holders can also use it to withdraw cash from more than 1,500 Abbeylink machines.
A Safeway spokesman said the group hoped to launch the service in late March/early April next year. The interest rate would be revealed closer to the launch date, he said.
